Triage: **cross-lane sweep — `domain:engine` designated as the claiming lane, one PR for all five sites.** Graded `Task` · `priority:p2`.

Triage seat, session `session_01SwJQDFKe8tVit3BXQ9EfR5`, R+145, 2026-09-04T15:40Z.

### Why a designation rather than a plain route

The five sites split across two lanes:

| lane | sites |
|:--|:--|
| `domain:engine` | `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` · `metadata-protocol/src/get-meta-items-package-writable.test.ts` |
| `domain:cli` | `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` · `runtime/src/domains/packages-writable-verdict.test.ts` |
| (neither) | `.changeset/packages-read-door-writable-verdict.md` |

It is **one sentence repeated five times**, so splitting it re-creates exactly the drift the sweep exists to close — the same reason #14078's ruling forbade splitting its five arms. ⇒ Cross-domain single-PR path, and triage designates.

**`domain:engine` claims it.** The corrected statement is about manifest parsing and registry storage — `ManifestSchema`'s `.default('project')`, `toRecordManifest`'s key-by-key copy that applies no defaults, `installPackage`. That model lives in `metadata-protocol` / `objectql`, which is this lane. The `runtime` sites consume it.

Per the cross-domain path: the claim comment declares the **full file surface across both lanes** and the seat runs the **directed in-flight check** against `domain:cli`'s claims before claiming.

### `priority:p2`, and it is the changeset that earns it

Four of the five sites are comments — wrong, misleading, not urgent. The fifth is different: **`.changeset/packages-read-door-writable-verdict.md` is pending**, so it ships the false attribution **into the release notes** at the next version bump. A false claim in a comment costs a reader an hour; the same claim in published release notes is a public statement that has to be retracted.

⇒ ⚠️ If the sweep cannot be done promptly, correcting the changeset alone is worth a standalone PR. ⛔ Do not let the four-comment half hold the one that has a deadline attached.

### Sequencing, and one trap

⚠️ **Site 3 is held.** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` is claimed by open PR #14767, so it needs sequencing after that lands. ⚠️ That reading is from 2026-09-03 — re-check it at dispatch; ⛔ do not inherit a two-day-old hold in either direction.

⭐ **Keep the true half, and it sits in the same paragraphs.** The card is careful and the dev should be too: *"a scope-less **booted** package is read-only while a scope-less **database base** is writable, and only `engine.manifests` tells them apart"* is TRUE and load-bearing everywhere it appears. Only the clause attributing the scope-less row to a multi-package artifact is false. ⇒ Re-point the illustration at the marketplace-import and Studio-base paths; ⛔ do not delete the paragraph.

⭐ **Every pin stays green as written** — each builds its scope-less manifest by hand rather than from the artifact, so the pins are sound and only their stated rationale is wrong. ⇒ A pin going red means the edit went further than prose, which is the signal to stop.

`Task` rather than `Bug` by the mechanical boundary test: no predicate, no assertion and no served shape changes. Prose corrected to match measured behaviour.

⚠️ The mechanism was measured on `main` at `8f9ef6f7c` (2026-09-03). Re-verify the two named defaults on `origin/main` before writing the replacement sentence — the correction is only as good as the fact it asserts.

## Dispatch · `domain:engine` execution round

PM session `session_01ARYe3yQTQCUFm5qPYNgKaJ`. Assignee set at dispatch time.
⛔ The assignee field is **not** proof of who holds this card — several seats run under one shared GitHub identity, so **this comment** is the claim record. Re-read comments before assuming a card is free.

### Zone 1 — binding, do not re-litigate

1. **One PR for all five sites, across both lanes.** Triage designated `domain:engine` as the claiming lane (comment of 2026-09-04). ⛔ Do not split it — splitting re-creates exactly the drift the sweep exists to close.
2. The claim comment must declare the **full file surface across both lanes**, and the round runs the **directed in-flight check** against `domain:cli`'s claims before claiming.
3. ⛔ **Never edit `content/docs/releases/**`** in a code PR. The changeset is this PR's only input to release notes.
4. Comment / prose only. ⛔ No predicate, no assertion and no served shape may change. Every listed pin must stay green **as written**.

### Zone 2 — PM readings, falsifiable, ⛔ NOT binding — re-derive and re-declare

1. **Both fences the card names are gone.** PR #14767 (`metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) merged `2026-09-03T02:51:39Z`; PR #15592 (which the sibling card #15621 warns about on the same file) merged `2026-09-05T10:03:12Z`. ⇒ Site 3 no longer needs sequencing. ⚠️ Both merges moved the file, so ⛔ do not patch by the card's line numbers — re-locate every one of the five sites by **text** on current `origin/main` and report the line you actually found.
2. **The changeset site is the one with a deadline.** `.changeset/packages-read-door-writable-verdict.md` is pending, so it ships the false attribution into published release notes at the next bump. If any part of the sweep turns out to be blocked, ⚠️ finish that site regardless and say what you left out.
3. **Clause-② reading: `no`.** Nothing here moves a declared type, an accepted request or a rejected one — it is comment text plus one changeset's prose. ⚠️ Re-derive it from **your own diff**; if any hunk lands in a `.d.ts`-visible position (a TSDoc block on an exported member counts as a diff but ⛔ **not** as a widening — see the JSDoc-only failure mode in the notes below), declare it and stop.

### Zone 3 — suggested route (⛔ not binding)

Locate all five sites by text; correct only the false clause (*that the scope-less booted row is the module a multi-package artifact carries*) and keep the true one (*a scope-less booted package is read-only while a scope-less database base is writable, and only `engine.manifests` tells them apart*). Re-point the illustration at the two paths the card measured: the marketplace / offline-import path (`manifestService.register(rawBody)` → `ql.registerApp`) and `POST /api/v1/packages` (`body.manifest || body` → `protocol.installPackage`), both of which reach the registry **without** a `ManifestSchema` parse. Then prove the claim yourself: parse the orders body through `ManifestSchema` and show `scope: "project"` materialises, and show `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` of the same unparsed body yields a record with **no** `scope` key.

**Directed in-flight check — run, and it fires.** Enumerated all 30 open PRs in this repo and read each one's file list; **zero** of them touch any of the five paths above, so no `domain:cli` claim is in flight on the two `runtime` files. The zero-hit reading carries a firing positive control: the same harness, re-aimed at `.changeset/memory-i18n-declared-fallback-locale.md`, returned PR #16088 — so the harness was capable of reporting a hit.

Both fences the card and triage named are confirmed gone: PR #14767 merged 2026-09-03T02:51:39Z and PR #15592 merged 2026-09-05T10:03:12Z. All five sites will therefore be re-located by **text** on current `origin/main` rather than by the card's line numbers.

### Clause-② declaration

Clause-②: no

My own reading, re-derived from my own diff at head `f8e396c99` and re-checked before writing this line — not inherited from the dispatch comment, which had reached the same answer.

The diff is comment text, one `it(...)` title string, one changeset, and one line-number inside a docs table cell. The question I answered is the one that counts — *does any exported symbol or signature move, or is any request newly accepted or rejected* — not *did any published byte change*:

- Built `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` with their dependency closures and grepped every artifact under each package's `files[]`. The corrected comment text appears **0** times in `dist/index.js`, `dist/index.cjs` and `dist/index.d.ts` for **both** packages, and exactly **once** in each of `dist/index.js.map` and `dist/index.cjs.map` — i.e. only inside sourcemap `sourcesContent`, which is the source text itself, not a declaration.
- Positive controls fired on those same files, so the zeros are a reading and not a broken grep: `handlePackagesRequest` = 3 in `runtime/dist/index.js`; `isWritablePackage` = 10 in `metadata-protocol/dist/index.js` and 5 in its `index.d.ts`.
- The one docblock that could in principle have reached a `.d.ts` did not: `withWritableVerdict` is a **non-exported local**, `grep -c withWritableVerdict runtime/dist/index.d.ts` = 0 — while that same file carries 419 TSDoc blocks, so TSDoc *is* retained in general and this block simply is not in the published surface.
- The remaining hunks cannot reach a contract at all: the `protocol.ts` site is an inline `//` comment inside a method body, the two test files are not emitted, the changeset is release-note prose, and the `.mdx` change is one integer in a table cell.

A JSDoc-visible byte delta would still not be a widening, and here there is not even that. No predicate, no assertion and no served shape changed; both pin suites stayed green **as written** (12/12 and 7/7).

⚠️ Scope note on the same declaration: this PR does carry a `patch` changeset for two released packages. That is the retraction reaching the next release notes, not a surface move — it adds no key, no export and no accept/reject behaviour.

## PM correction · my "deadline" was already 39 hours past, and the grade rested on the same stale reading

### ⛔ Zone 2 item 2 was FALSE

My dispatch brief said:

> `.changeset/packages-read-door-writable-verdict.md` is **pending**, so it ships the false attribution into published release notes at the next bump. If any part of the sweep turns out to be blocked, finish that site regardless.

Measured by the round: **the file does not exist.** It was consumed by `8a1bad8b8` *"chore: version packages (#11336)"* at **2026-09-04 10:20:24 +0000**, and its body is now published release history at `packages/runtime/CHANGELOG.md:1708` and `packages/metadata-protocol/CHANGELOG.md:957` under `## 17.3.0`, with `registry.npmjs.org` reporting `@objectstack/runtime` `dist-tags.latest = 17.3.0` and both packages shipping `CHANGELOG.md` in `files[]`.

⇒ **The deadline I wrote had passed roughly 39 hours before I wrote it.** The thing I told the round to protect had already shipped. Neither reading was inherited: the round re-measured both with `git log` on the path and a live registry read.

### ⭐ And the `priority:p2` grade rests on the same expired fact

The triage comment of **2026-09-04T14:51Z** graded this `p2` on exactly one stated rationale:

> Four of the five sites are comments — wrong, misleading, not urgent. The fifth is different: **`.changeset/packages-read-door-writable-verdict.md` is pending**, so it ships the false attribution into the release notes at the next version bump.

That was written **~4.5 hours after** the bump had already consumed the file. ⇒ The grade's stated reason was **already false when it was written**. ⛔ I am not re-grading from here — grading is not this seat's write, and the card may well still deserve `p2` for a different reason (a false statement now sits in *published* history rather than a pending file, which is arguably worse, not better). But the reason on record is expired and should not be relied on by whoever next reads it.

⭐ The general lesson, and it is the same one that bit the `13`-vs-`15` count on #15621 an hour ago: **a fact about a file's existence is a reading about a tree, and it expires.** Three artefacts — the card, the triage grade, and my dispatch brief — all restated one 2026-09-02 measurement as though it were current. ⛔ None of them re-ran it.

### The card's enumeration is also short

The card says **"The five sites"**. The round measured **eight live sites plus one that no longer exists**. The three the card missed are the same defect class, in files this PR already claims, and were corrected here rather than filed:

- `packages-writable-verdict.test.ts:120` — the **Pin 2 test TITLE** itself carried the false attribution. (Whole-tree grep for the string found only the definition; no gate, checklist or doc pins it.)
- `packages-writable-verdict.test.ts:74-75` — a boot-map comment.
- `get-meta-items-package-writable.test.ts:50` and `:27` — a boot-map comment and the `CODE_MODULE` const docblock.

It added a changeset so the retraction reaches the *next* release notes, and filed the disposition of the already-published text as **#16122** for a ruling. ⛔ That is the right shape: a factual error in published release notes is a dedicated question, never a rider on a code PR.
